title: Loose Rein state.yaml (rein-grounded-v1)
description: Mutable state only. Task titles, dependencies, and claim mappings live in the frozen plan — duplicating them here is how two documents drift apart. Written exclusively by the Central Store's transaction; no command edits this file directly.

sources.description: The prose the implementation phase reads — the task tickets and the design/requirements documents — digested at the gate ③ freeze, keyed by repo-relative path. plan.yaml is frozen with a digest; the documents an implementer is actually sent to read were bound to nothing, so a ticket edited after the freeze changed what got built with no record that it had. Worse, a parallel leaf is cut from the work branch's tip and reads only what is committed, so an *uncommitted* edit changed nothing at all and said nothing either.

review.description: Digests of the current review. `human_digest` is null until the human section is frozen; a mismatch between any of these and a recomputed value makes the review stale (plan 17.5).

tasks.description: Per-task mutable status, keyed by the task id declared in plan.yaml. A key with no matching plan task is a cross-reference error.

status.description: `awaiting-evidence` is neither a failure nor a completion: the task's acceptance criteria include evidence this loop cannot obtain (a staging check, a device, a person), so nothing has judged it. It sits off the frontier until a human records the observation with `rein evidence record`.

acceptance.description: Acceptance criteria established outside this loop, each bound to the tree it was observed against — so an observation cannot outlive the code it was about, the same rule every other piece of evidence here follows. Written by `rein evidence record` from the canonical checkout only: an agent that can record its own acceptance has not been checked by anyone.

note.description: What was observed, and where. A human reads this beside the gate ④ decision.

evidence.description: Why this task is done — the auditable half of the evidence ledger. `done` used to mean "the implementer process exited and the gate was green", which a task that changed nothing satisfied. It now means "these steps were established green against exactly this tree", and the tree is a content fingerprint, so a verdict cannot outlive the code it was about. Written in the same transaction that marks the task done; the reuse half of the ledger is a disposable cache outside the working tree and is never consulted for this.

tree.description: The content fingerprint the verdict was reached on (HEAD + tracked modifications + untracked blobs).

base.description: What that tree is a change to.

steps.description: The quality-gate steps established green against that tree, in the order they ran.

image.description: The pinned image the step ran in — "make test was green" is not a fact about the code alone.

reused.description: True when the ledger already held this exact fact and the step was not re-run.

acceptance.description: The task's own acceptance criteria established against that tree, and how each one was.

reported.description: What the implementer said about its own work, before anything was checked. Kept beside the verified facts rather than instead of them.

handoff.description: What the next attempt at this task inherits from the interrupted one. The implementer's own agent session dies with the terminal that ran it, so this — not a session id — is what survives a crash: which gate step failed, what it said, how much retry budget is actually left, where the preserved work-in-progress went, and what the last agent launch actually said before it stopped.

failed_step.description: The quality-gate step the previous attempt could not get green.

failure_summary.description: The tail of that step's output, as the next implementer is told it.

retries_left.description: Remaining send-back budget per step name. Absent means the step's configured budget is untouched; restoring it is what stops a crash loop from getting infinite retries.

salvage_branch.description: The branch an interrupted run's unmerged work was preserved on.

salvage_state.description: What became of that branch on the next attempt: still waiting to be picked up, merged into the fresh worktree, or left behind because merging it conflicted.

report.description: What the last implementer said, in its own words, through `rein report`. A claim, not a verdict: the loop checks `touched` against the real diff and treats a disagreement as a finding. Its value is diagnostic — an implementer that stopped because its own sandbox refused to let it write says so here, instead of the run degrading to "the tree did not change" with no reason attached.

touched.description: The paths the implementer says it changed.

review.description: What the independent reviewer said about the last attempt. Carried so the next launch reads it instead of the reviewer re-deriving the same objection, and so `consider` findings — which stop nothing — still reach the human at gate ④ rather than dying with the session that produced them.

last_agent.description: Diagnostics from the last agent launch for this task — never a verdict about it. The loop used to discard a successful launch's output entirely, so an implementer that reported "blocked: my sandbox will not let me write" reached the human as nothing at all.

last_fault.description: The last environment fault this task hit. Recorded precisely because it is *not* a verdict: no status changes and no retry budget is spent, so without this the reason would exist only in a terminal that has since closed.

change_requests.description: Changes a human asked for instead of approving. Human-authored, mutable, and it has to outlive the session that raised it — which is why it lives here and not in a chat message.

gate.description: Which gate this request stands against.

target.description: What in the deliverable this is about: a document anchor (docs/10-requirements.md#R-3) or an id (R-3, C-001, T-004). The anchor is the point — it is what lets the fix read one slice instead of re-running the phase.

status.description: open: blocks the gate. addressed: the agent says it is answered and names how; no longer blocks, but is listed on the approval screen so the human reads it before deciding. resolved: closed by the gate approval that covered it.

gate.description: A gate is `approved` only with a receipt binding the human confirmation, the deliverable digests, and the event chain root at the moment of approval. There is no path to `approved` without one — plan 16.0.

approval_id.description: The id `rein approve` minted for this confirmation. It appears in the gate_approved event's subjects too, so the receipt and the audit record cannot disagree about what was approved.

confirmed_via.description: Which channel carried the human's confirmation: a terminal, or a dashboard write session (which exists only by redeeming the launch secret printed on the server's terminal). Never a claim about *who* — both say only that something with access to this machine's terminal did it.
